indications.drug:
Diuretics
definition and fluid balance
indications.text: Diuretics increase urine flow and/or sodium and chloride excretion. A sustained imbalance between sodium and chloride intake and loss is fatal: too much means volume overload and pulmonary edema; too little means volume depletion and cardiovascular collapse.
indications.edu: The goal is balance, never maximum fluid removal: the same drug that clears a congested lung can empty the circulation if over-used.

indications.drug:
Diuretic braking
how the kidney fights back
indications.text: The kidneys receive about a fifth of the cardiac output, so they defend their blood flow. Counter-regulation ("diuretic braking") includes activation of the sympathetic nervous system and the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, a lower blood pressure (less pressure natriuresis), a lower atrial natriuretic peptide with a higher antidiuretic hormone, and renal cell hypertrophy.
indications.edu: This counter-regulation is why a diuretic's effect fades over time.

indications.drug:
Filtration
glomerulus
indications.text: Glucose, sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate and amino acids are all filtered. About 150 to 180 liters are filtered a day but only 1 to 2 liters are excreted, so most of what is filtered is reabsorbed further down the nephron.
indications.edu: A diuretic only needs to block a small fraction of reabsorption to change urine output a great deal.

indications.drug:
Proximal tubule
site of reabsorption
indications.text: Reabsorbs glucose, amino acids and organic solutes; weak acids and bases are excreted into the lumen. 60 to 70 percent of the filtrate is reabsorbed here (carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act in this segment).
indications.edu: Where a drug acts predicts what it does to potassium, calcium and acid-base balance: learn the segment first.
verify: Reabsorption of Glucose, amino acids and organic solutes
Weak acids and bases excreted into lumen

indications.drug:
Loop of Henle
concentrates the urine
indications.text: Concentrates urine and reabsorbs sodium. Descending limb: water leaves the lumen. Ascending limb: about 25 percent of sodium is reabsorbed and the limb is impermeable to water. Loop diuretics work at this site.
indications.edu: Blocking this limb removes about a quarter of the filtered sodium, and the segments downstream cannot reabsorb enough to make up for it, so it gives the largest diuresis.
verify: Ascending loop: 25% of Na+ reabsorbed, impermeable to water
Loop diuretics work at this site

indications.drug:
Distal tubule
site of thiazides
indications.text: About 5 percent of sodium is reabsorbed here. Thiazide diuretics act at this site. Added background: aldosterone mainly drives sodium and potassium handling in the late distal tubule and collecting duct; antidiuretic hormone controls the water channels of the collecting duct.
indications.edu: Thiazides act after the loop, which is why they are weaker than loop diuretics.

indications.drug:
Collecting duct
site of potassium-sparing drugs
indications.text: 2 to 3 percent of sodium is reabsorbed; antidiuretic hormone controls the water channels, while aldosterone controls sodium and potassium handling. Potassium-sparing diuretics act at this site.
indications.edu: Aldosterone pulls sodium in and pushes potassium out here; blocking it (or the sodium channels it controls) is what spares potassium.
verify: Water movement controlled by Aldosterone and ADH

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Inhibit the sodium-potassium-2 chloride carrier on the luminal membrane of the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle. Four agents: furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide and ethacrynic acid.
indications.edu: Class before agent: if a stem describes this carrier or the thick ascending limb, the class is loop diuretic. Ethacrynic acid does not follow the naming pattern of the others, so learn it by name.
verify: Inhibit the Na-2Cl-K carrier on the luminal membrane of the thick ascending loop of Henle

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Major actions: inhibit sodium chloride reabsorption by 20 to 25 percent; raise urine output by up to 4 liters a day; increase potassium excretion; increase calcium and magnesium excretion.
indications.edu: Know the effect on each electrolyte: loops lower potassium, calcium and magnesium. A stem asking which diuretic lowers calcium is asking for a loop diuretic.
verify: Increase urine output up to 4 liters/day

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Pulmonary edema, nephrotic syndrome (protein loss disrupts fluid regulation), cirrhosis of the liver (ascites), hypercalcemia (used with saline), heart failure, renal failure or insufficiency and hypertension.
indications.edu: Reach for a loop diuretic whenever a lot of fluid must come off. Hypercalcemia is treated with a loop diuretic plus saline because loops increase calcium excretion.

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Loop diuretics are effective in patients with a creatinine clearance below 30 milliliters per minute. Thiazides classically lose effect at low clearance (metolazone is the exception).
indications.edu: Added background: a patient who is still making urine on a loop diuretic does not necessarily have good kidney function, because the drug can force urine out of poorly working kidneys.
verify: Loops effective in patients with creatinine clearance rates below 30 ml/min
Thiazides are ineffective at low creatinine clearance rates
Metolazone effective at lower clearance rates

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Systemic vasodilator actions: loop diuretics stimulate prostaglandins (prostaglandin E2), an effect blocked by nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and have a direct relaxant effect on muscle (mechanism not understood).
indications.edu: This is the reason nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs blunt a loop diuretic's effect.

verify: NSAIDS - blunt the natriuretic and blood pressure response

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Interaction: nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs blunt the natriuretic and blood pressure response. Interaction: aminoglycosides potentiate ototoxicity.
indications.edu: Ask about over-the-counter pain relievers; a patient whose "water pill" stopped working may be taking one. Avoid stacking ear-toxic drugs.
verify: NSAIDS - blunt the natriuretic and blood pressure response

indications.drug:
Loop diuretics
furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid
indications.text: Interaction: lithium (clearance falls, toxicity rises). Interaction: warfarin (the two compete for plasma protein binding). Interaction: digitalis (potassium and magnesium loss raise the risk of arrhythmias).
indications.edu: Loop diuretics lower potassium and magnesium, which is the setup for digoxin toxicity; check electrolytes in anyone taking both.
verify: Warfarin - compete for plasma protein binding

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Inhibit the sodium-chloride transporter in the luminal membrane of the distal convoluted tubule (the major action). Agents: chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone and indapamide.
indications.edu: Class before agent: a distal-tubule sodium-chloride transporter blocker is a thiazide.
verify: Inhibit Na/CL transporter in luminal membrane of DCT (major)

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Increase sodium chloride excretion (up to 5 percent of the filtered load) and urine output (1 to 2 liters a day); increase potassium and magnesium excretion; decrease renal calcium excretion (the opposite of loop diuretics).
indications.edu: Calcium is the contrast to memorize: loops waste calcium, thiazides keep it.
verify: inhibits up to 5% of filtered NaCl

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Calcium-containing kidney stones (calcium oxalate): by holding calcium back from the urine, thiazides leave less to crystallize. Added background: thiazides raise serum calcium, so they cause hypercalcemia rather than treat it (loop diuretics with saline treat it).
indications.edu: Counter-intuitive but true: serum calcium may rise slightly while urine calcium, and so stone formation, falls.

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Hypertension, renal failure, cirrhosis of the liver and congestive heart failure. In heart failure, thiazides are generally not potent enough, and loop diuretics are used instead.
indications.edu: Thiazides are standard drugs for blood pressure but are not the drugs for large fluid overload.

verify: Not potent enough for most HF patients

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Low-dose thiazides are preferred for hypertension, with few adverse effects. They work best in elderly patients, African American patients and sodium-retentive states. Short term they lower blood volume and cardiac output; chronically they lower total peripheral resistance (direct vasorelaxant effects, less sodium in arteriolar walls, less "waterlogging").
indications.edu: Patients with hypertension who retain sodium respond best. Added background: thiazides are the diuretic usually chosen for long-term blood pressure control; loop diuretics are kept for fluid overload and advanced kidney disease.
verify: Low dose thiazides preferred for hypertension, few adverse effects
Works best in 1) elderly, 2) obese, 3) African Americans, 4) sodium retentive states

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Thiazides classically lose effect when creatinine clearance is low (below about 30 to 40 milliliters per minute); metolazone remains effective at lower clearance. Added background: newer trial data show that chlorthalidone can still lower blood pressure in advanced chronic kidney disease.
indications.edu: Added background: metolazone is the thiazide added to a loop diuretic when a patient with poor kidney function still needs more diuresis.
verify: Thiazides are ineffective at low creatinine clearance rates
Metolazone effective at lower clearance rates

indications.drug:
Thiazide diuretics
chlorothiazide, hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone, metolazone, indapamide
indications.text: Interaction: nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs block prostaglandins and weaken the natriuretic action. Interaction: digitalis: thiazides increase digitalis toxicity, so potassium should be kept above 4.0 mEq per liter.
indications.edu: Check the potassium of anyone taking a thiazide and digoxin together.
verify: NSAIDS - block PG's attenuate natriuretic actions

indications.drug:
Potassium-sparing diuretics
amiloride, triamterene
indications.text: Block luminal sodium channels in the collecting duct. They inhibit 2 to 3 percent of sodium chloride reabsorption, decrease the gradient for potassium secretion (so potassium is spared) and give a modest increase in urine flow.
indications.edu: These are weak diuretics used for what they do to potassium, not for volume.

indications.drug:
Potassium-sparing diuretics
amiloride, triamterene
indications.text: Amiloride and triamterene are the two agents; both are sold as fixed combinations with hydrochlorothiazide.
indications.edu: A combination product contains a thiazide as well, so it lowers sodium and keeps potassium at once.

indications.drug:
Potassium-sparing diuretics
amiloride, triamterene
indications.text: Same uses as the other diuretics but much less natriuretic and diuretic effect. Most often used in combination with other diuretics or antihypertensive drugs.
indications.edu: Their main job is to offset the potassium lost with loop diuretics and thiazides. Added background: salt substitutes are usually potassium chloride, so a patient on a potassium-sparing diuretic should check with the prescriber before using one.
verify: Same as others but much less natriuretic and diuretic effects
Most often used in combination with other diuretics or antihypertensive drugs

indications.drug:
Aldosterone
normal actions
indications.text: Aldosterone binds its receptor, which translocates to the nucleus and activates protein synthesis: more sodium channels in the membrane and more activity of the sodium-potassium adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase) pump, with more energy production in the distal convoluted tubule.
indications.edu: More sodium channels means more sodium and water retained and more potassium lost; excess aldosterone therefore causes low potassium.
verify: Binds to receptor translocated to nucleus

indications.drug:
Aldosterone antagonists
spironolactone, eplerenone
indications.text: Spironolactone and eplerenone bind the steroid (aldosterone) receptor but the complex does not translocate to the nucleus, so aldosterone's actions are blocked. Most effective when aldosterone is high; they block 2 to 3 percent of sodium chloride reabsorption and reduce potassium loss; modest effect on lipids, glucose and uric acid.
indications.edu: The drug is a receptor antagonist, so it needs aldosterone to be present to matter: it works best in states of high aldosterone.
verify: Binds to steroid receptor but does not translocate to nucleus

indications.drug:
Aldosterone antagonists
spironolactone, eplerenone
indications.text: Primary aldosteronism, hypertension, heart failure (advanced; see the heart failure section), edematous conditions, cirrhosis (secondary hyperaldosteronism) and nephrotic syndrome.
indications.edu: Both a diuretic and a survival drug in advanced heart failure. In the heart failure section the same drug class is described for class III or IV failure; learn it as advanced failure.

verify: Mortality reduction in grade III or IV HF

indications.drug:
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
acetazolamide, dichlorphenamide, methazolamide
indications.text: Inhibit carbonic anhydrase: bicarbonate absorption in the proximal tubule falls by 80 to 90 percent, so less hydrogen ion is produced and less sodium-hydrogen exchange occurs. Short-term effect: sodium and potassium excretion rises about 5 percent; after 3 to 5 days the effect falls to 1 to 3 percent.
indications.edu: These are the weakest diuretics because the rest of the nephron makes up for the loss. Bicarbonate is trapped in the tubule and lost in the urine.
verify: Long term (after 3-5 days) effect is reduced to 1-3 %

indications.drug:
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
acetazolamide, dichlorphenamide, methazolamide
indications.text: Acetazolamide, dichlorphenamide and methazolamide.
indications.edu: Class before agent: three agents, all ending in -zolamide or -phenamide.

indications.drug:
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors
acetazolamide, dichlorphenamide, methazolamide
indications.text: Other uses: glaucoma (lowers bicarbonate in the ciliary body; dorzolamide and brinzolamide), epilepsy (metabolic acidosis, central nervous system effects) and mountain (altitude) sickness.
indications.edu: Used as diuretics rarely; their value is in these other uses. Added background: for altitude sickness the metabolic acidosis makes the patient breathe faster, which helps at low oxygen pressure.

indications.drug:
Heart failure
etiology
indications.text: Ischemic heart disease and myocardial infarction cause 50 to 60 percent of cases. Other causes: hypertension, idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, other cardiomyopathies (alcoholic, viral, hypertrophic) and drug-induced failure.
indications.edu: Treating blood pressure and coronary disease helps prevent heart failure.

indications.drug:
Heart failure
systolic dysfunction
indications.text: Systolic dysfunction is decreased contractility from loss of myocardial muscle mass, left ventricular hypertrophy or dilated cardiomyopathy. It is assessed as a reduced ejection fraction.
indications.edu: Systolic failure is the type the survival drugs (ACE inhibitors, three beta blockers, aldosterone antagonists) were proved in.

indications.drug:
Heart failure
diastolic dysfunction
indications.text: Diastolic dysfunction is impaired relaxation: thicker, stiffer ventricles relax less well, and ischemia impairs removal of calcium from the cytosol back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Ventricular filling falls, so cardiac output falls, with symptoms despite a preserved ejection fraction.
indications.edu: A normal ejection fraction does not rule out heart failure.
verify: Thicker, stiffer ventricles relax less efficiently
Decreased ventricular filling, thus decreased cardiac output
HF symptoms with preserved ejection fraction

indications.drug:
Heart failure
compensatory response
indications.text: Compensation: increased preload (sodium and water retention), vasoconstriction, tachycardia and increased contractility from sympathetic activation, and left ventricular hypertrophy. These begin as help and become a vicious cycle: lower cardiac output drives neuroendocrine activation, sodium and water retention and a higher afterload.
indications.edu: Each drug class breaks one link of the cycle: diuretics lower preload, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors lower afterload, beta blockers blunt sympathetic drive.
verify: Increased preload (through Na and water retention)

indications.drug:
Heart failure
decompensation
indications.text: Common precipitants of decompensation: lack of compliance, uncontrolled hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, inadequate therapy, inappropriate medications or fluid overload, acute anginal chest pain, pulmonary infection and emotional stress.
indications.edu: Counsel on diet and medication adherence: missed medicines and salty or fluid-heavy meals are the commonest avoidable triggers.

indications.drug:
Heart failure
nonpharmacologic therapy
indications.text: Restrict dietary sodium and fluid; physical activity may improve functional status.
indications.edu: Tell the patient to limit salt and fluid and to stay active as tolerated.
verify: Physical activity may improve functional status

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Diuretics in heart failure
loop diuretics
indications.text: Loop diuretics are the mainstay of heart failure therapy: they decrease sodium and water retention and so lower preload, for symptomatic benefit. Thiazide diuretics are not potent enough for most patients with heart failure.
indications.edu: Loops relieve congestion and swelling; they are not what extends life.
verify: Decreases sodium and water retention thus decreasing preload
Not potent enough for most HF patients

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Diuretics in heart failure
what they do not do
indications.text: Diuretics are for symptomatic relief only. There is no evidence they decrease progression or mortality, and they are not mandatory therapy.
indications.edu: A drug that improves mortality stays on whatever the symptoms; a drug for symptoms only is not mandatory. Added background: some patients adjust the loop diuretic dose by their daily weight.
verify: Diuretics are for symptomatic relief only
No evidence to show they decrease progression or mortality

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Daily weight
monitoring fluid status
indications.text: Monitoring the patient's weight is a good way to detect worsening fluid overload. A gain over several days is fluid, not tissue.
indications.edu: Teach daily weights at the same time each morning and a clear rule for when to call; a rising weight means fluid is building up.
verify: Monitoring patient's weight is a good way to detect worsening fluid overload

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitors
in heart failure
indications.text: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors decrease preload, afterload and sympathetic activation and decrease left ventricular hypertrophy, dilation and remodeling, so they slow progression and decrease mortality. Patients should be on an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and a beta blocker irrespective of symptoms.
indications.edu: These are survival drugs: they stay on even when symptoms are controlled. Added background: angiotensin receptor blockers are the alternative when cough develops, and can be used with caution after angioedema.
verify: Decrease left ventricular hypertrophy, dilation, and remodeling
Patients should be on ACEI and BB irrespective of symptoms

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitors
in heart failure
indications.text: Benefits: hemodynamic improvement, improved exercise tolerance, decreased heart failure symptoms, fewer hospital admissions, slowed progression of disease and prolonged survival.
indications.edu: The benefit list is the reason to keep titrating the drug up to the target tolerated amount.

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Beta blockers in heart failure
carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol
indications.text: Beta blockers were classically considered contraindicated in heart failure. The three with a mortality benefit are carvedilol, metoprolol succinate (extended release) and bisoprolol.
indications.edu: Only these three: other beta blockers have not been shown to lower mortality in heart failure. The succinate (extended-release) metoprolol is the one that lasts all day.
verify: Classically considered contraindicated in heart failure

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Beta blockers in heart failure
carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol
indications.text: Keys to successful use: the patient should be stable before initiation (hospital initiation was traditionally preferred); start with very low doses and titrate up slowly (over several weeks); monitor for worsening heart failure signs and symptoms.
indications.edu: "Low and slow": starting too fast or in an unstable patient can worsen heart failure. Tell the patient that benefit builds over months and that symptoms may briefly worsen.
verify: Patient should be stable prior to initiation
Titrate up slowly over 6-8 weeks total
Monitor for worsening HF signs and symptoms

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Beta blockers in heart failure
carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol
indications.text: Benefits: improved exercise tolerance, hemodynamic improvement (increased ejection fraction), slowed disease progression, fewer hospitalizations, less need for transplant and decreased mortality.
indications.edu: Like angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, these are survival drugs rather than symptom drugs.

indications.group: Heart failure: diuretics, ACE inhibitors and beta blockers
indications.drug:
Beta blockers in heart failure
carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol
indications.text: First-line therapy in class II to IV heart failure. Patients should be on an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor and a beta blocker irrespective of symptoms.
indications.edu: Anyone with systolic heart failure should be on both unless contraindicated or not tolerated.
verify: First line therapy in Class II-IV heart failure
Patients should be on ACEI and BB irrespective of symptoms

indications.drug:
Digoxin
cardiac glycoside
indications.text: A lactone ring and a steroid nucleus are essential for activity; the sugar molecules influence absorption, half-life and metabolism.
indications.edu: Digoxin is a cardiac glycoside: steroid core, lactone ring and sugars.
verify: Lactone ring and Steroid nucleus essential for activity
Sugar molecules influence absorption, half-life and metabolism

indications.drug:
Digoxin
cardiac glycoside
indications.text: Inotropic action (the older mechanism): digoxin inhibits the sodium-potassium adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase); intracellular sodium rises, so intracellular calcium rises through the sodium-calcium exchanger and the fiber shortening (force of contraction) increases.
indications.edu: Block the sodium pump, retain sodium, bring in calcium, contract harder: this is a positive inotrope.

verify: Increase force of cardiac muscle contraction

indications.drug:
Digoxin
cardiac glycoside
indications.text: Neurohormonal actions (the newer mechanism): decreased sympathetic and increased parasympathetic activity, resensitized baroreflex, lower heart rate, more parasympathetic activity at the atrioventricular node, and decreased renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system activity, so less remodeling, better perfusion and higher cardiac output.
indications.edu: Part of the benefit is a slower heart rate that lets the ventricles fill for longer.
verify: Decrease sympathetic and Increase parasympathetic nervous system activity
parasympathetic activity in AV node and conduction system

indications.drug:
Digoxin
cardiac glycoside
indications.text: Clinical benefits: improved symptoms, exercise tolerance and quality of life, and fewer hospitalizations. No survival benefit.
indications.edu: Digoxin is a symptom drug: it is never mandatory, unlike angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and the three beta blockers.

indications.drug:
Digoxin
cardiac glycoside
indications.text: Place in therapy: no evidence of slowed disease progression; primary use is in symptomatic patients already on optimal angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, beta blocker and diuretic therapy; considered in symptomatic heart failure with systolic dysfunction; can be used for rate control in atrial fibrillation with heart failure. Added background: it is generally an add-on, not the first drug for rate control.
indications.edu: Add it when a patient is still symptomatic on the survival drugs. Added background: because it is cleared by the kidneys, kidney disease makes it accumulate.
verify: No evidence of slowed disease progression
Primary use in symptomatic patients on optimal doses of ACE inhibitors/beta blockers and diuretics
Considered in patients with symptomatic HF and systolic dysfunction

indications.drug:
Digoxin
cardiac glycoside
indications.text: Target blood level 0.5 to 1 ng/mL; higher concentrations may be associated with worse outcomes in heart failure.
indications.edu: A narrow target range is why digoxin is one of the few heart failure drugs monitored with a drug level.
verify: Higher concentrations may be associated with worse outcomes in HF patients

indications.drug:
Digoxin immune Fab
antidote
indications.text: Digoxin immune Fab is an antibody fragment that binds digoxin (affinity for digoxin is higher than digoxin's affinity for the sodium-potassium adenosine triphosphatase (ATPase)); it is produced by immunizing healthy sheep with digoxin coupled to human serum albumin, and it rapidly reverses toxicity.
indications.edu: This is the antidote for life-threatening toxicity. Added background: removing the digoxin can unmask the atrial fibrillation or heart failure it was treating.
verify: Antibody which binds to the antigen-binding site of Ig
immunization of healthy sheep with digoxin coupled to human serum albumin
Affinity higher for Digoxin than affinity of digoxin and Na+K+ ATPase

indications.drug:
Aldosterone antagonists in heart failure
spironolactone, eplerenone
indications.text: Spironolactone gives a mortality reduction in advanced (class III or IV) heart failure. Patients are not eligible if potassium is above 5 or serum creatinine is above 2.5. Gynecomastia occurs in about 10 percent of men. Eplerenone has less effect on androgen receptors and does not usually cause gynecomastia. Mechanism: neurohormonal inhibition, slowed remodeling of the left ventricle and slowed progression of heart failure.
indications.edu: Check potassium and kidney function before and during treatment. If a man on spironolactone develops breast enlargement, switching to eplerenone avoids it.
verify: Mortality reduction in grade III or IV HF
Patients not eligible if K > 5 or SCr > 2.5
Neurohormonal inhibition, slowed remodeling of LV
Eplerenone has less effect on androgen receptors

indications.drug:
Phosphodiesterase (type III) inhibitors
milrinone, inamrinone
indications.text: Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cyclic AMP) phosphodiesterase (type III) inhibitors. Inotropic and vasodilator actions: direct stimulation of myocardial contraction, balanced arterial and venous dilation, decreased afterload and increased cardiac output.
indications.edu: Both a stronger squeeze and a lower afterload. Added background: because they also dilate vessels, they suit acute failure with an adequate blood pressure rather than a low one.
verify: Inotropic as well as vasodilator actions

indications.drug:
Phosphodiesterase (type III) inhibitors
milrinone, inamrinone
indications.text: Approved for short-term intravenous use in acute decompensated heart failure. Long-term use is associated with higher mortality and morbidity than placebo.
indications.edu: These are in-hospital stabilizing drugs, transitioned off once the patient is stable and on usual oral therapy; they are never for long-term use.
verify: Approved for short term IV use in acute decompensated heart failure
Long term use is associated with higher mortality and morbidity

indications.drug:
Dobutamine and dopamine
intravenous inotropes
indications.text: Dobutamine is a selective beta-1 agonist: intravenous infusion stimulates the force of contraction more than the rate; short-term use to stabilize patients. Dopamine is given by intravenous infusion and acts through dopamine and beta receptors.
indications.edu: Added background: when decompensation comes with low blood pressure, an agent that does not rely on vasodilation, such as dobutamine, is generally favored over milrinone; low-dose dopamine has not been shown to protect kidney function.
verify: IV infusions stimulates force of contraction more than rate of contraction
Short term use to stabilize patients
Actions through dopamine and beta receptors

indications.drug:
Ivabradine
hyperpolarization-activated channel blocker
indications.text: Blocks the hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel, inhibiting the pacemaker current in the sinoatrial node: reduces heart rate without affecting contractility. Used in heart failure patients maxed out on beta blockers, in normal sinus rhythm with a heart rate above 70 beats per minute; decreases hospitalization and heart failure related death.
indications.edu: Add-on only: it replaces neither the beta blocker nor the angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor; it needs a regular sinus rhythm.
verify: Inhibits pacemaker current in SA node
Reduces heart rate, doesn't affect contractility
Used in CHF patients who are maxed out on beta blockers
Shown to decrease hospitalization and HF related death

indications.drug:
Sacubitril-valsartan
neprilysin inhibitor with an angiotensin receptor blocker
indications.text: Sacubitril is a neprilysin inhibitor, formulated with valsartan. Neprilysin normally degrades vasoactive peptides (natriuretic peptide, bradykinin); inhibition causes vasodilation, natriuresis and diuresis and inhibits growth and fibrosis of myocardial tissue. Used to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization in heart failure.
indications.edu: It carries an angiotensin receptor blocker, so it takes the place of an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or receptor blocker.
verify: Normally responsible for degrading vasoactive peptides
Inhibition causes vasodilation, natriuresis, and diuresis
Inhibits growth and fibrosis of myocardial tissue
Used to reduce risk of CV death and hospitalization in patients with CHF

indications.drug:
Sacubitril-valsartan
neprilysin inhibitor with an angiotensin receptor blocker
indications.text: Do not use along with an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, and give a 36-hour washout period to avoid adverse effects.
indications.edu: When switching from an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, stop it and wait 36 hours before the first sacubitril-valsartan.
verify: Don't use along with ACE inhibitor and give 36 hour washout period to avoid adverse effects

indications.drug:
Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors
dapagliflozin, empagliflozin
indications.text: Dapagliflozin and empagliflozin are indicated for stable, chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, where they reduce mortality and hospitalizations. Originally developed for diabetes: they make the kidneys not reabsorb glucose.
indications.edu: The patient will pass glucose in the urine; counsel on hydration and on genital and urinary hygiene. Added background: these drugs are also used in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
verify: Causes kidneys to not reabsorb glucose

sideeffects.drug:

charts.title: Diuretics Compared by Site of Action
charts.sub: The five diuretic classes in order down the nephron: where each works, how, how strong it is, what it does to potassium, calcium and magnesium, what else it changes, what it is for, what it causes and what it interacts with.
headers: Sodium chloride inhibited and urine output
charts.notes: Read the potency column top to bottom. Where the drug acts predicts its strength: the thick ascending limb handles about a quarter of the filtered sodium, the distal tubule about 5 percent and the collecting duct 2 to 3 percent. Know the potassium effect of every row: loops, thiazides and carbonic anhydrase inhibitors lower potassium; potassium-sparing diuretics and aldosterone antagonists raise it. Calcium splits the loops from the thiazides: loops waste calcium (used for hypercalcemia), thiazides hold on to it (fewer calcium stones). All of them share the volume-depletion side effects (reflex activation of the renin-angiotensin system, aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone, contraction alkalosis, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia); the weaker the diuretic, the milder these are. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors are the one class that causes an acidosis. (Added background: furosemide, bumetanide and ethacrynic acid carry a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) boxed warning for profound diuresis, and amiloride and triamterene for hyperkalemia.)

charts.sub: Every heart failure drug class side by side, sorted by the question that matters most: does it only relieve symptoms, or does it help the patient live longer? Then where it fits, what it causes and what to watch.
charts.notes: The rule behind the third column: a drug that improves survival is one the patient needs on board whatever the symptoms; a drug that only relieves symptoms may not be needed all the time. Survival: angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, the three named beta blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), aldosterone antagonists in advanced failure, sacubitril-valsartan (reduces cardiovascular death) and the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors. Symptoms only: diuretics, digoxin, milrinone and inamrinone, dobutamine. Ivabradine lowers hospitalization and heart failure death. Wording not repeated as written: some summaries call digoxin first line for atrial fibrillation with heart failure, which is overstated (it is an option for rate control); weight-gain, sodium, fluid, titration-time and ejection fraction cut-off numbers are left as qualitative statements (the current cut-off for reduced ejection fraction is 40 percent or below, not 45). (Added background: ACE inhibitors and sacubitril-valsartan carry a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) boxed warning for fetal toxicity; a beta blocker is not stopped abruptly.)

charts.title: Digoxin: Action, Toxicity and Antidote
charts.sub: Everything about digoxin in one place, in the order a patient meets it: what it is, how it works, what it does and does not do, who gets it, how toxicity shows up, what raises the risk and how it is reversed.
charts.notes: Three things to carry out of this chart: digoxin relieves symptoms but does not improve survival; its toxicity clue is yellow-green halos (with nausea, confusion and bradycardia); and low potassium, low magnesium and high calcium raise the risk. Wording not repeated as written: some lists of contraindications name high potassium, and some summaries call digoxin first line for atrial fibrillation with heart failure. The established risk is low potassium (hyperkalemia is not a risk factor for toxicity, though a very high level of potassium accompanies severe acute poisoning), and digoxin is an option, not the first choice, for rate control. The target level is shown for reference only; recognizing toxicity matters more than the number.

cells: What it is

cells: Older mechanism: inotropic

Inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase, so intracellular sodium rises; the sodium-calcium exchanger then lets calcium accumulate and fiber shortening (contraction) increases. It increases the force of cardiac muscle contraction.

verify: Increase force of cardiac muscle contraction

Lower sympathetic and higher parasympathetic activity (lower heart rate, more atrioventricular nodal slowing), resensitized baroreflex, less renin-angiotensin-aldosterone activity, less remodeling and better tissue perfusion; cardiac output rises.

Nodal slowing (longer PR interval, shorter QT interval, depressed ST segment), bradycardia (most common), and digoxin-induced after-depolarizations that cause ventricular arrhythmias such as premature ventricular beats.

A loop diuretic plus a potassium-sparing diuretic is a common deliberate pairing to offset potassium loss. (Added background: potassium chloride salt substitutes add potassium.)
